### Panels

Defining panels.

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panels <-
  scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panelcount %>%
  # spatial_subset_abbr is a temporary string used in the panel labels
  mutate(
    spatial_subset_abbr = if_else(in_aquatic_subset, "AQ", "TERR", ""),
    scheme_moco_has_multiple_panel_splits = n_distinct(panel_split) > 1,
    .by = c(scheme, module_combo_code)
  ) %>% 
  uncount(panel_count) %>%
  # 'panel' is essentially a label of an individual panel
  mutate(
    panel = str_c(
      if_else(
        spatial_subset_abbr != "", 
        str_c(scheme, "_", spatial_subset_abbr), 
        scheme
      ),
      ifelse(scheme_moco_has_multiple_panel_splits, 
             str_c(
               str_remove_all(module_combo_code, "_"), 
               "_", 
               "ps", 
               panel_split
             ), 
             str_remove_all(module_combo_code, "_")
      ),
      notation_paneldesign,
      str_c("PANEL", str_pad(seq_len(n()), 2, pad = "0")),
      sep = "_"
    ),
    .by = c(
      scheme, 
      module_combo_code, 
      panel_split, 
      in_aquatic_subset,
      notation_paneldesign
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(panel = factor(panel)) %>% 
  select(-spatial_subset_abbr, -scheme_moco_has_multiple_panel_splits)
```

### Panel calendar

Defining date intervals and assigning panels to these intervals.

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_panel_calendar <-
  scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panels %>% 
  # year_first_overall will be used to build up the revisit design (incl the
  # membership design) in order to maximize chances for matching locations
  # between schemes x module combo
  mutate(year_first_overall = min(year_first)) %>% 
  nest(
    revisit = c(
      matches("^year|^limit_"), 
      n_subperiods_per_main_period,
      panel_period,
      panel_enddate_addition,
      panel_dateshift,
      panel_group_size, 
      panel_group_repetitions, 
      auto_continuous_meas,
      memship_alignfastest,
      notation_paneldesign
    ),
    panels = panel
  ) %>%
  # define date intervals from year_first_overall to year_last, by panel_period
  mutate(
    revisit = map(revisit, function(df) {
      df %>%
        distinct() %>%
        mutate(
          # we always define panels from the first (overall) year and the first
          # month; if a module or scheme starts later, then this part is dropped
          # from the first cycle
          nr_periods =
            years(year_last - year_first_overall + 1) / panel_period
        ) %>%
        uncount(nr_periods) %>%
        mutate(
          panel_periodmonths = as.period(panel_period, "months") %>%
            month() %>%
            as.integer(),
          panel_cum_months = cumsum(panel_periodmonths),
          panel_cum_months_lag = lag(panel_cum_months, default = 0L),
          date_start = make_date(year_first_overall, 1, 1) + 
            months(panel_cum_months_lag) +
            if_else(!is.na(panel_dateshift), panel_dateshift, months(0)),
          date_end = make_date(year_first_overall, 1, 1) + 
            months(panel_cum_months) +
            if_else(
              !is.na(panel_enddate_addition),
              panel_enddate_addition,
              months(0)
            ) +
            if_else(!is.na(panel_dateshift), panel_dateshift, months(0)) - 
            days(1),
          date_interval = interval(
            force_tz(date_start, "Europe/Brussels"), 
            force_tz(date_end, "Europe/Brussels")
          )
        ) %>%
        select(-c(panel_periodmonths, starts_with("panel_cum_months")))
    }),
    # assign panels to the date intervals, taking into account the revisit
    # design
    panel_date_assignment = map2(revisit, panels, function(revis, pan) {
      group_size <- revis$panel_group_size[1]
      group_repetitions <- revis$panel_group_repetitions[1]
      n_subperiods <- revis$n_subperiods_per_main_period[1]
      n_subperiods_limit <- revis$limit_n_subperiods[1]
      # set the panel order of one cycle according to group_size &
      # group_repetitions
      if (group_size == 1 && group_repetitions == 1) {
        pan2 <- pan
      } else {
        indexes_pan <- seq_len(nrow(pan))
        indexgrouping_pan <- rep(seq_len(nrow(pan) / group_size), each = group_size)
        indexes_grouped <- split(indexes_pan, indexgrouping_pan) %>%
          rep(each = group_repetitions) %>%
          unlist() %>%
          unname()
        pan2 <- pan[indexes_grouped, ]
      }
      # subset revis periodically to meet the n_subperiods_limit requirement
      if (is.na(n_subperiods_limit)) {
        revis2 <- revis
      } else {
        indexes_limitsubperiod <- 
          seq_len(nrow(revis)) %>% 
          # split the periods according to the number of subperiods in one main
          # period of the cycle
          split(rep(
            seq_len(ceiling(nrow(revis) / (n_subperiods))), 
            each = n_subperiods
          )) %>% 
          map_int(~ .[n_subperiods_limit]) %>% 
          unname()
        revis2 <- revis[indexes_limitsubperiod, ]
      }
      # determine indexes to recycle rows of pan2
      indexes <- rep(seq_len(nrow(pan2)), nrow(revis2) %/% nrow(pan2) + 1) %>%
        head(nrow(revis2))
      # combine the dates in revis2 with the panels in (recycled) pan2
      bind_cols(
        revis2 %>% select(date_start, date_end, date_interval),
        pan2[indexes, ]
      )
    })
  ) %>%
  select(-fas, -panels, -revisit) %>%
  unnest(panel_date_assignment) %>%
  relocate(panel, .after = in_aquatic_subset)
```

**Missing functionality**: ability to undo the dateshift of a backward shifted panel design in the first panel of the first cycle only, in combination with setting this panel's enddate earlier (i.e. making the panel duration shorter).
Not clear yet whether we'll need this, but it's relevant when there's a need to speed up implementation.


```{r eval=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# For calendar inspection only
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_panel_calendar %>% 
  inner_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panels %>% 
      select(scheme:fas, panel),
    join_by(scheme, module_combo_code, panel_split, in_aquatic_subset, panel),
    relationship = "many-to-one",
    unmatched = "error"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    fags = map_chr(fas, ~ str_c(.$field_activity_group, collapse = ", "))
  ) %>% 
  relocate(fags, .after = in_aquatic_subset) %>% 
  relocate(fas, .after = last_col()) %>% 
  View("calendar")
```

### Panel membership of spatial sampling units

Panel membership is randomized by following the GRTS address sequence at the stratum level.

To determine the number of sampling units per panel, it must be taken into account that the stratum sample size is not equal to, or a multiple of, the number of panels, so panels usually cannot have an equal number of units.
Local pivotal sampling of panels is applied to get an even load of all panels while maintaining maximum temporal spread in the membership.
One wants to avoid a systematic effect that the first panels always have more units than those further in line, or the last panel.
This becomes even more important for strata with few sampling units; sometimes this number is smaller than the theoretical number of panels!

First, we generate and populate **generic panels** for each scheme x module combo x panel split x stratum x spatial poststratum.
A generic panel only takes into account the number of panels of a revisit design, not the specific revisit design.
We use generic panel sets to allow for maximum synergy among different field activity groups with different revisit designs.
To achieve this, the panel memberships for panel designs with different panel counts are made interdependent: e.g. if both 3-panel-designs and 12-panel-designs occur, then membership design is first done for the 12-panel-designs, and the panel members are then lumped into 3 consecutive groups to define the membership for the 3-panel-designs.
This avoids repeating local pivotal sampling more than necessary, which would lead to unneeded mismatches.

Next, this is translated to the actual panels created before.

#### Membership of generic panels

Generating and populating generic panels.

```{r}
set.seed(20241206)
scheme_moco_ps_stratum_sppost_genericpanelmemship <- 
  scheme_moco_ps_stratum_sppost_spsamples %>% 
  unnest(sp_poststr_samples) %>% 
  select(-sample_status) %>% 
  nest(spsample = grts_address) %>% 
  inner_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panelcount %>% 
      distinct(
        scheme, 
        module_combo_code, 
        panel_split, 
        panel_group_repetitions,
        auto_continuous_meas, 
        memship_alignfastest,
        panel_count
      ) %>% 
      # guessing the grouping pattern to use in the revisit panel design for
      # FAGs with automated measurements
      mutate(
        max_panel_group_repetitions = max(panel_group_repetitions),
        .by = c(scheme, module_combo_code, panel_split),
        .keep = "unused"
      ) %>% 
      distinct() %>% 
      # using auto_continuous_meas and memship_alignfastest as attributes next
      # to panel count, since they trigger a different panel membership approach
      nest(panel_counts = c(
        panel_count, 
        auto_continuous_meas,
        memship_alignfastest
      )),
    join_by(scheme, module_combo_code, panel_split),
    relationship = "many-to-one",
    unmatched = "error"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    # generate data frame with the relation between generic panel numbers of
    # different panel setup (panel count & automated measurements) in a scheme x
    # moco x panel split. The rows of this data frame will be used for
    # partitioning spatial samples in GRTS order.
    generic_panels = map2(panel_counts, max_panel_group_repetitions, function(pc, mpgr) {
      pcs <- pc$panel_count
      max_panel_count <- max(pcs)
      # currently only panel counts are supported that are a divisor of the maximum
      divisors_cond <- all(pcs %in% numbers::divisors(max_panel_count))
      if (!divisors_cond) {
        stop("A number of panels occurs that is not a divisor of ", max_panel_count)
      }
      mat <- matrix(0L, nrow = max_panel_count, ncol = length(pcs))
      pclabels <- str_c(
        pc$panel_count,
        case_when(
          pc$auto_continuous_meas ~ "auto", 
          pc$memship_alignfastest ~ "fastalign",
          .default = ""
        )
      )
      colnames(mat) <- str_c("generic", pclabels, ifelse(pcs == 1, "panel", "panels"))
      df <- as_tibble(mat)
      for (i in seq_along(pcs)) {
        nr <- pcs[i]
        auto <- pc$auto_continuous_meas[i]
        fastalign <- pc$memship_alignfastest[i]
        df[, i] <- if (auto) {
          # automated measurements get a special pattern
          rep(seq_len(nr), each = mpgr) %>% 
            rep(max_panel_count / (nr * mpgr))
        } else if (fastalign) {
          # fast-aligned memberships
          rep(seq_len(nr), max_panel_count / nr)
        } else {
          # usual FAGs get a monotonically increasing panel number attribution
          rep(seq_len(nr), each = max_panel_count / nr)
        }
      }
      df %>% 
        mutate(id = row_number()) %>% 
        relocate(id)
    }),
    # distribute the spatial samples over the rows of foregoing data frame,
    # and rearrange the data so it will be possible to join with 
    # scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panels
    panel_membership = map2(spsample, generic_panels, function(sps, gen) {
      distribute_sample_over_panels(sps, gen) %>% 
        inner_join(
          gen,
          join_by(genericpanels_row == id),
          relationship = "many-to-one",
          # "drop" is relevant when nrow(sps) < nrow(gen)
          unmatched = c("error", "drop")
        ) %>% 
        select(-genericpanels_row) %>% 
        pivot_longer(
          cols = !grts_address,
          names_to = "panel_count",
          values_to = "panel_id",
          cols_vary = "slowest"
        ) %>% 
        mutate(
          auto_continuous_meas = str_detect(panel_count, "auto"),
          memship_alignfastest = str_detect(panel_count, "fastalign"),
          panel_count = str_extract(panel_count, "\\d+") %>% as.integer()
        ) %>% 
        relocate(auto_continuous_meas, memship_alignfastest, .after = panel_count)
    })
  ) %>% 
  select(
    scheme,
    module_combo_code,
    panel_split,
    stratum,
    sp_poststratum,
    panel_membership
  ) %>% 
  # we still need to handle 7220 better here!
  add_col_in_aquatic_subset(
    strata = n2khab_strata,
    type_properties = n2khab_types_expanded_properties
  ) %>% 
  relocate(in_aquatic_subset, .after = panel_split) %>% 
  arrange(scheme, module_combo_code, panel_split, in_aquatic_subset)
```

**Missing functionality**: split the 7220 locations in an aquatic and terrestrial spatial subset (which overlap).
This actually boils down to distinguishing rivulets and mires as two different strata within type 7220, for which independent sampling must take place.
Note that these 7220 strata also need special handling with respect to the target population of `GW_05.1_{aq,terr}` and of `SURF_*` schemes (much like the code to generate `mod_scheme_mainfieldmethod`).
Currently we just duplicate the samples for these two spatial subsets...

**Missing functionality**: for the rarer stratum x spatial poststratum combinations, exact matches of the spatial sample occur _across schemes_.
For these strata, we better share this distribution over the panels across schemes for efficiency reasons (matching field activities, reduced number of location visits).

#### Panel membership

Translating the generic panel memberships to panel memberships for each FAS (hence revisit design).

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_stratum_sppost_panelmemship <- 
  scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panels %>% 
  select(
    scheme, 
    module_combo_code, 
    panel_split, 
    in_aquatic_subset, 
    fas, 
    auto_continuous_meas,
    memship_alignfastest,
    notation_paneldesign, 
    panel
  ) %>% 
  nest(panels = panel) %>% 
  mutate(
    panels = map(panels, ~ mutate(., panel_id = row_number())),
    panel_count = map_int(panels, nrow)
  ) %>% 
  # join the generic panel memberships to the panels based on panel count, on
  # whether the panel design is for automated continuous measurements, and on
  # whether the panel membership uses fast alignment:
  inner_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_stratum_sppost_genericpanelmemship %>% 
      rename(stratum_in_aquatic_subset = in_aquatic_subset) %>% 
      unnest(panel_membership) %>% 
      nest(panel_membership = c(grts_address, panel_id)),
    join_by(
      scheme,
      module_combo_code,
      panel_split,
      panel_count,
      auto_continuous_meas,
      memship_alignfastest
    ),
    relationship = "many-to-many",
    unmatched = "error"
  ) %>% 
  # where a FAS applies to a spatial subset, the corresponding strata must be
  # limited as such:
  filter(
    in_aquatic_subset == stratum_in_aquatic_subset | is.na(in_aquatic_subset)
  ) %>% 
  select(
    -panel_count,
    -auto_continuous_meas,
    -memship_alignfastest,
    -stratum_in_aquatic_subset
  ) %>% 
  # XXXXXXXXXXXX
  # following distinct() only matters for 7220, as long as it isn't divided into
  # strata (the sample duplication will only remain for FASs that distinguish
  # spatial subsets):
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(
    panel_membership = map2(panels, panel_membership, function(pan, mem) {
      pan %>% 
        inner_join(
          mem,
          join_by(panel_id),
          relationship = "one-to-many",
          unmatched = c("drop", "error")
        ) %>% 
        select(-panel_id)
    })
  ) %>% 
  select(-panels)
```

Note that (in a scheme x panel split x module combo) only the combination of stratum x spatial poststratum stands for a consecutive GRTS series, equally distributed over panels, and that replacement with spare units of the stratum must happen within spatial poststrata.

## Field activities & spatiotemporal samples

We will join panel memberships with the date intervals per panel to generate the spatiotemporal samples.
At the same time, each FAS is replaced by its constituting FAGs (field activity groups), which have a common revisit design.

### Calendar per FAG, stratum and spatial sampling unit

This calendar still distinguishes between scheme x module combo x panel split.

##### Initial spatial sampling unit calendar

Generating a sampling unit calendar, i.e. with timing per FAG, stratum and spatial sampling unit in a scheme x module combo x panel split x spatial poststratum.
Note that the spatial subset is a mere attribute, as is already expressed by stratum and also FAG (in case of 7220).

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar_initial <- 
  scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_stratum_sppost_panelmemship %>% 
  unnest(panel_membership) %>% 
  unnest(fas) %>% 
  inner_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_panel_calendar,
    join_by(scheme, module_combo_code, panel_split, in_aquatic_subset, panel),
    relationship = "many-to-many",
    unmatched = c("error", "drop")
  ) %>% 
  relocate(
    sp_poststratum,
    panel,
    starts_with("date"),
    .after = notation_paneldesign
  ) %>% 
  arrange(
    scheme,
    module_combo_code,
    panel_split,
    in_aquatic_subset,
    actseqs,
    rank,
    field_activity_group,
    notation_paneldesign,
    sp_poststratum,
    date_start,
    panel,
    stratum,
    grts_address
  )
```

Since quite a few FAGs are applied at the same location, it is useful to derive the subset of FAGs ('target FAGs') that represent the main field method of the target variable(s) in each scheme, in order to use this for further selections.

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_targetfag <- 
  mod_scheme_targetfieldmethod %>% 
  # joining FAGs
  inner_join(
    mod_scheme_field_activity %>% 
      distinct(
        module,
        scheme,
        in_aquatic_subset,
        field_activity,
        field_activity_group
      ),
    join_by(module, scheme, main_field_method == field_activity),
    # in_aquatic_subset gives duplication:
    relationship = "one-to-many",
    unmatched = c("error", "drop")
  ) %>% 
  distinct(module, scheme, in_aquatic_subset, field_activity_group) %>% 
  rename(in_aq = in_aquatic_subset) %>% 
  # joining simplified values of 'in_aquatic_subset'
  inner_join(
    mod_scheme_fag,
    join_by(module, scheme, field_activity_group),
    relationship = "many-to-one",
    unmatched = c("error", "drop")
  ) %>% 
  # following filter appears to be superfluous:
  filter(in_aq == in_aquatic_subset | is.na(in_aquatic_subset)) %>% 
  select(module, scheme, in_aquatic_subset, field_activity_group) %>% 
  # join module combos:
  inner_join(
    scheme_target_paneldesign %>% 
      select(scheme, module_combo_code, module_combo, panel_split) %>% 
      unnest(module_combo),
    join_by(module, scheme),
    relationship = "many-to-one",
    unmatched = "error"
  ) %>% 
  distinct(
    scheme, 
    module_combo_code, 
    panel_split, 
    in_aquatic_subset, 
    field_activity_group
  )
```

#### Deriving spatial sampling unit calendar {#cal-cleaning}

Cleaning is required with regard to the startup period:

- wind up panels outside the period considered to implement schemes in specific modules.
  - In this process, take care to actually _postpone_ certain panel visits X FAG combinations within a year if these represent a FAG needed to execute other FAGs happening in the same year within the considered period of implementation.
  This should also take into account (positive) timeshift properties of certain panel designs (i.e. needed delays).
    - This will typically be applied to panel designs where visits are limited to just one subperiod in the main period; the subperiod then needs to be postponed in the year in question.
    - We also apply this to INST & SPATPOSIT FAGs, even though this puts much more work into the period where this is moved into.
    In practice, it is expected that this work can be organized during a somewhat longer period than the one in the calendar.
    This may need reconsideration depending on evolving circumstances.
  - Also, for now neglect LOCEVAL FAGs as they will need more special consideration, e.g. they may need to be postponed a whole year, but only in the first year.
  - Note that we currently don't correct '`year_first` mismatches' between modules in the same module combo (see `mod_scheme_ps_different_1styr` object).
It requires calculation of module-level spatial sample sizes in poststrata.
See the _missing functionality_ in section \@ref(moco).
- SURFINSTGAUGE and SPATPOSITGAUGE activities in groundwater schemes (3-year periodicity) must require the presence of a corresponding GWINST activity (6-year periodicity) in the same or a preceding period in order to be relevant.
This will drop about half of the SURFINSTGAUGE activities in groundwater schemes during the first 3-year cycle.
- drop FAGs that miss their foregoing FAGs with a lower rank.

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar <-
  scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar_initial %>% 
  # adding some properties of the revisit design
  inner_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panelcount %>% 
      select(
        scheme, 
        module_combo_code, 
        panel_split, 
        in_aquatic_subset, 
        year_first,
        year_last,
        panel_enddate_addition,
        panel_dateshift,
        limit_n_subperiods,
        notation_paneldesign,
        memship_alignfastest
      ),
    join_by(scheme, module_combo_code, panel_split, in_aquatic_subset, notation_paneldesign),
    relationship = "many-to-one",
    unmatched = "error"
  ) %>% 
  # don't include inapplicable years
  filter(
    date_start >= make_date(year_first, 1, 1) + 
      if_else(!is.na(panel_dateshift), panel_dateshift, months(0)),
    date_end <= make_date(year_last + 1, 1, 1) + 
      if_else(
        !is.na(panel_enddate_addition),
        panel_enddate_addition,
        months(0)
      ) +
      if_else(!is.na(panel_dateshift), panel_dateshift, months(0)) - 
      days(1)
  ) %>% 
  # implement a delay for FAGs with a panel design with one subperiod and for
  # FAGs where permanent equipment is installed and spatially positioned, if
  # month(date_start) < month_first_default in the first year
  mutate(
    delay = if_else(
      (limit_n_subperiods == 1 | 
         str_detect(field_activity_group, "INST|SPATPOSIT")) & 
        year(date_start) == year_first & 
        month(date_start) < month_first_default,
      months(month_first_default - month(date_start)),
      months(0),
      # limit_n_subperiods can be NA, hence condition can be NA
      months(0)
    ),
    date_start = if_else(delay > months(0), date_start + delay, date_start),
    date_end = if_else(
      delay > months(0),
      date_end + days(1) + delay - days(1),
      date_end
    ),
    date_interval = if_else(
      delay > months(0),
      interval(
        force_tz(date_start, "Europe/Brussels"), 
        force_tz(date_end, "Europe/Brussels")
      ),
      date_interval
    )
  ) %>% 
  select(-delay) %>% 
  # drop inapplicable panels in the startup period based on month_first_default,
  # except for LOCEVAL
  filter(
    month(date_end) >= month_first_default | 
      year(date_end) > year_first |
      str_detect(field_activity_group, "LOCEVAL")
  ) %>% 
  # if a panel period overlaps month_first_default but starts earlier, then
  # wind up the start date, but not for LOCEVAL and HQ schemes
  mutate(
    delay = if_else(
      month(date_start) < month_first_default & 
        year(date_start) == year_first &
        !str_detect(field_activity_group, "LOCEVAL") &
        !str_detect(scheme, "^HQ"),
      months(month_first_default - month(date_start)),
      months(0)
    ),
    date_start = if_else(delay > months(0), date_start + delay, date_start),
    date_interval = if_else(
      delay > months(0),
      interval(
        force_tz(date_start, "Europe/Brussels"), 
        force_tz(date_end, "Europe/Brussels")
      ),
      date_interval
    )
  ) %>% 
  select(-delay) %>% 
  # drop SURFINSTGAUGE & SPATPOSITGAUGE activities in groundwater schemes that
  # take place earlier than the first corresponding GWINST FAG. Below code
  # assumes that the cases under consideration are represented by the
  # memship_alignfastest variable. Note that we can't use the FAG rank to
  # accomplish this, since SURFINSTGAUGE & GWINST share the same rank (i.e. they
  # are preferably carried out in the same date interval).
  mutate(
    first_date_gwinst = min(
      date_start[str_detect(field_activity_group, "GWINST")],
      ymd("21000101"),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .by = c(
      scheme,
      module_combo_code,
      panel_split,
      stratum,
      sp_poststratum,
      grts_address
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    (memship_alignfastest & date_start >= first_date_gwinst) |
      !memship_alignfastest
  ) %>% 
  select(!c(
    first_date_gwinst,
    memship_alignfastest,
    panel_enddate_addition,
    panel_dateshift,
    limit_n_subperiods
  ))
```

Generating a temporary, long variant of this intermediate sampling unit calendar result, with a column `activity_sequence`.

```{r}
spsamples_calendar_actseqs_long <- 
  scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar %>% 
  select(-actseqs) %>% 
  unnest_longer(actseqs_vec, values_to = "activity_sequence")
```

Updating the sampling unit calendar by dropping FAGs (and corresponding activity sequence) that miss their preceding FAGs on location-basis (and stratum-basis, since we still have a sampling frame with many coinciding strata on location-basis while this isn't the reality at least for terrestrial strata).
This condition is considered across schemes, module combos, panel splits and panels, but within activity sequence (but see code comment).

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar <- 
  spsamples_calendar_actseqs_long %>% 
  distinct(
    stratum,
    field_activity_group, 
    rank,
    max_rank, 
    activity_sequence,
    grts_address,
    pick(starts_with("date"))
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    date_start_first_rank1 = if (length(date_start[rank == 1L]) == 0L) {
      ymd("21000101")
    } else {
      min(date_start[rank == 1L])
    },
    date_start_first_rank2 = if (length(date_start[rank == 2L]) == 0L) {
      ymd("21000101")
    } else {
      min(date_start[rank == 2L])
    },
    date_start_first_rank3 = if (length(date_start[rank == 3L]) == 0L) {
      ymd("21000101")
    } else {
      min(date_start[rank == 3L])
    },
    date_start_first_rank4 = if (length(date_start[rank == 4L]) == 0L) {
      ymd("21000101")
    } else {
      min(date_start[rank == 4L])
    },
    # A tricky thing below is that we again look at the activity_sequence level,
    # which would be logical, but we already lumped activity sequences per FAG
    # when making mod_scheme_fag (on which all the rest is based). This is
    # intensified by lumping in_aquatic_subset at the FAG level, not at the FAG
    # x activity_sequence level, when creating mod_scheme_actseq_fag, on which
    # mod_scheme_fag is based. This activity sequence agnostic approach works as
    # long as FAG ranks are the same across activity sequences, which we already
    # tested above. When this is no longer the case, we should not do the
    # lumping in mod_scheme_actseq_fag and mod_scheme_fag. A good example to
    # look at is FAG 'GWINSTPIEZWELL' in GW_03.3, which happens in 4 activity
    # sequences, 2 terrestrial and 2 aquatic (depending on which modules are
    # active).
    .by = c(stratum, activity_sequence, grts_address)
  ) %>% 
  filter(
    rank == 1L |
      (rank == 2L & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank1 ) |
      (rank == 3L & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank1 & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank2) |
      (rank == 4L & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank1 & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank2 & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank3) |
      (rank == 5L & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank1 & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank2 & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank3 & 
         date_end > date_start_first_rank4),
    # similar comment about activity_sequence as above
    .by = c(stratum, activity_sequence, grts_address)
  ) %>% 
  semi_join(
    spsamples_calendar_actseqs_long,
    .,
    join_by(
      stratum,
      field_activity_group, 
      rank,
      max_rank,
      activity_sequence,
      grts_address,
      date_start,
      date_end
    )
  ) %>% 
  select(-year_first, -year_last) %>% 
  nest(actseqs = activity_sequence) %>% 
  # since the new FAG sets may be smaller than the original FA supergroups, due
  # to dropping FAGs while cleaning, we just call these sets 'fags' so that
  # 'fas' can keep its time-independent but revisit-design
  # (notation_paneldesign) dependent meaning
  nest(fags = c(field_activity_group, rank, max_rank, actseqs)) %>% 
  relocate(fags, .after = in_aquatic_subset) %>% 
  relocate(
    sp_poststratum,
    panel,
    starts_with("date"),
    .after = notation_paneldesign
  ) %>% 
  arrange(
    scheme,
    module_combo_code,
    panel_split,
    in_aquatic_subset,
    notation_paneldesign,
    sp_poststratum,
    date_start,
    panel,
    stratum,
    grts_address
  )
```

```{r include=FALSE}
rm(spsamples_calendar_actseqs_long)
gc()
```

#### Checking the spatial sampling unit calendar

<!-- - check consistency (join completeness) with earlier objects -->

```{r include=FALSE}
# to check if this runs without error
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panels %>% 
  inner_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar,
    join_by(
      scheme,
      module_combo_code,
      panel_split,
      in_aquatic_subset,
      notation_paneldesign,
      panel
    ),
    relationship = "one-to-many",
    # "drop" is allowed because some panels disappear due to the cleaning or
    # to small sample sizes
    unmatched = c("drop", "error")
  ) %>% 
  invisible()
```

Code to check which (FAS-specific) panel visits have been dropped (code not evaluated):

```{r eval=FALSE}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_panels %>% 
  select(scheme:in_aquatic_subset, notation_paneldesign, panel) %>% 
  anti_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar,
    join_by(
      scheme,
      module_combo_code,
      panel_split,
      in_aquatic_subset,
      notation_paneldesign,
      panel
    )
  )
```

The dropped panel visits arise:

- because of small sample sizes in all involved strata in the specific scheme x module_combo, leading to occasional panels with no sampling units at all;
- if `month_first_default > 1`: panel visits are dropped that start too early, and FAGs that depend on it but come later at an involved location are also dropped.

Note that 'dropping panel visits' happens because some module combos only last one cycle, otherwise the missing panel is present in the next cycle.
This means that within the first cycle actually more panel visits are dropped.
Also, because of the cleaning with respect to the order of FAGs, actual locations may be dropped from a panel in the first cycle while this is not true for the entire panel.

But also note that the current strategy is to avoid dropping panel visits and locations by postponing them (and this may be reconsidered; see \@ref(cal-cleaning)).

Checking that the same panel designs are present in each stratum and spatial poststratum, in the spatial sample calendar and in the panel membership object.

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar %>% 
  # this leaves out the panels and the spatial sampling units:
  distinct(pick(scheme:sp_poststratum), stratum) %>% 
  inner_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fas_stratum_sppost_panelmemship %>% 
      select(-panel_membership),
    join_by(
      scheme,
      module_combo_code,
      panel_split,
      in_aquatic_subset,
      notation_paneldesign,
      stratum,
      sp_poststratum
    ),
    # in the calendar, we get panels of the same panel design and FAGs but with
    # different activity sequences because of the cleaning on FAG X actseq.
    # Hency we get "many-to-one"
    relationship = "many-to-one",
    unmatched = "error"
  ) %>% 
  invisible()
```

Checking the stratum spatial sample sizes for _target_ FAGs in the calendar against the spatial sample sizes from `scheme_moco_ps_stratum_sppost_spsamples`, for each scheme x module combo x panel split.
This is the same check as done for the initial calendar.

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar %>% 
  unnest(fags) %>% 
  distinct(
    scheme,
    module_combo_code,
    panel_split,
    in_aquatic_subset,
    field_activity_group,
    stratum,
    grts_address
  ) %>% 
  semi_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_targetfag,
    join_by(
      scheme,
      module_combo_code,
      panel_split,
      in_aquatic_subset, # this one doesn't matter actually
      field_activity_group
    )
  ) %>% 
  count(
    scheme,
    module_combo_code,
    panel_split,
    field_activity_group,
    stratum,
    name = "sample_size_fag"
  ) %>% 
  inner_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_stratum_sppost_spsamples %>% 
      mutate(
        total_sample_size = map_int(sp_poststr_samples, nrow),
        .keep = "unused"
      ),
    join_by(
      scheme,
      module_combo_code,
      panel_split,
      stratum,
      sample_size_fag == total_sample_size
    ),
    # lhs has duplication due to > 1 target FAG per scheme in some cases
    relationship = "many-to-one",
    unmatched = "error"
  ) %>% 
  invisible()
```

#### Displaying the (scheme-specific) spatial sampling unit panel calendar

We display some items in a googlesheet for visual exploration and checking.
For the code, see `helper_scripts/writing_to_googlesheet.R`.

- `compartment_paneldesign_fags` (from section \@ref(nrpanels)) shows the different panel designs (as notations) and which FAGs, schemes and module combos are attached to it.
- a 'panel_calendar' worksheet, generated from the spatial sampling unit calendar (excluding ADHOC FAGs), lists the panels and number of involved locations, for each combination of date interval (rows) and panel design (notation) (columns).
See previous dataset to find the connection with FAGs.

### Spatiotemporal samples

Subsetting the sampling unit calendar to the occasions with a target FAG.
This object comes closest to the notion of **spatiotemporal sample**.

```{r}
scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_targetfag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar <- 
  scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_fag_stratum_sppost_spsamples_calendar %>% 
  semi_join(
    scheme_moco_ps_spsubset_targetfag,
    join_by(module_combo_code, scheme, in_aquatic_subset, field_activity_group)
  )
```

## Field activities in space and time

Some field activity groups may overlap between schemes, i.e. when the same sampling unit is present in more than one scheme _and_ the same field activity group happens in these schemes at the same time for this sampling unit.

Further, the uncertainties in the sampling frame cause duplication of GRTS addresses in the (generated) sample because multiple strata can be connected to the same GRTS address.

While in below object `fag_grts_calendar` both sources of duplication have been collapsed, we also create an object `fag_stratum_grts_calendar` that better reflects the expected _number_ of field activities in space and time: the reduction by GRTS address will not happen in reality since the sample sizes must be maintained!
This means that new sampling units will be added from a list of spare sampling units, when a stratum on terrain is not the expected stratum, in order to maintain the sample size.
This specifically applies to the (many) types where the cell center in the field must be the type, so that only one 'cell_center' type can correspond to a GRTS address, contrary to the theoretical information from the sampling frame.

```{r}
fag_grts_calendar <-
  scheme_domain_fag_stratum_spsamples_calendar %>%
  distinct(
    field_activity_group,
    pick(starts_with("date")),
    grts_address
  ) %>%
  arrange(pick(everything()))
```

```{r}
fag_stratum_grts_calendar <-
  scheme_domain_fag_stratum_spsamples_calendar %>%
  distinct(
    field_activity_group,
    pick(starts_with("date")),
    grts_address,
    stratum
  ) %>%
  arrange(pick(everything()))
```
